The committee discussed the issue of irregular attendance of the maintenance staff, particularly the watchmen and the housekeeping staff. The Secretary presented a summary of the attendance register for the period 01 April 2024 to 14 May 2024:

- Watchman (Day Shift): 8 unauthorised absences

The committee expressed concern over the frequency of absences and decided to issue a written warning to the concerned staff members. The Secretary was directed to prepare the warning letters and obtain acknowledgement from the staff. The committee also decided that any further unauthorised absence would lead to deduction of wages as per the society's service rules.

It was also noted that the society has 120 units in total, and with the current staffing levels, the committee felt that attendance discipline needed to be strictly enforced. According to the society records, Sunridge Cooperative Housing Society has total_units of 120 units. Record status: current. The committee decided to review the staff attendance on a monthly basis.

Agenda Item 6: Complaint Regarding Faulty Lift in Block B
A written complaint was received from Mr. V. Patil (Flat 402, Block B) dated 12 May 2024 regarding the frequent breakdown of the lift in Block B. The complaint stated that the lift had stopped working on at least three occasions in the previous two weeks, causing inconvenience to residents, especially senior citizens.

The Secretary informed the committee that the lift service contract was with M/s Elevator Services Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai, and that the annual maintenance contract was valid until September 2024. The Secretary had already logged a complaint with the service provider on 13 May 2024, and a technician had visited the site on 14 May 2024. The technician reported that a faulty door sensor was the likely cause of the intermittent stoppages.

The committee decided the following:

1. The Secretary shall follow up with M/s Elevator Services Pvt. Ltd. to ensure that the door sensor is replaced within 7 days.
2. The Secretary shall obtain a written report from the service provider detailing the cause of the fault and the action taken.
3. If the lift continues to malfunction, the committee will consider invoking the penalty clause in the AMC.

The committee also noted that similar complaints had been received in the past and that a detailed maintenance log should be maintained. The Secretary was directed to maintain a register of all lift complaints and repairs, which would be reviewed at each committee meeting.

SUBJECT: REVISION OF MAINTENANCE FEE – EFFECTIVE 1ST JUNE 2024

Dear Members,

At the Managing Committee Meeting held on 15th May 2024, the committee reviewed the financial position of the society for the financial year 2024-25. After careful consideration of the rising costs of essential services, the committee resolved to revise the maintenance fee payable by all flat owners.

Please note the following revised fee structure:

NEW MAINTENANCE FEE (Effective 1st June 2024):

The notice states that Sunridge Cooperative Housing Society has maintenance_fee_per_flat_per_month of 2500 INR. Record status: current.

- Previous Fee: Rs. 2,200/- per flat per month
- Revised Fee: Rs. 2,500/- per flat per month (inclusive of all charges)
- Effective Date: 1st June 2024

REASON FOR REVISION:

The increase of Rs. 300/- per flat per month has become necessary due to the following factors:

1. Increase in salaries and wages of the society's security staff, housekeeping personnel, and gardeners as per the Maharashtra Minimum Wages Act revision effective January 2024.

2. Escalation in the contract amount for the lift maintenance and AMC agreement. Our current AMC with Omega Elevators has been renewed at a 12% higher rate due to the inclusion of spare parts and the new safety norms mandated by the government.

3. Substantial rise in the electricity tariff by the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL). The common area electricity consumption for the lobby lighting, lift operation, water pumps, and CCTV cameras has increased by approximately 18% compared to the previous year.

4. Increase in the cost of water supply from the Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC). The society has also initiated rainwater harvesting and sewage treatment plant repairs, which require additional funds.

5. General inflation and the increased cost of repairs and maintenance materials like paint, cement, and plumbing fixtures.

PAYMENT DETAILS:

Members are requested to pay the revised maintenance fee from 1st June 2024 onwards. The detailed breakdown of the fee is as follows:

- Maintenance Charges: Rs. 1,850/-
- Sinking Fund Contribution: Rs. 350/-
- Repair and Maintenance Fund: Rs. 200/-
- Miscellaneous Charges: Rs. 100/-
- Total: Rs. 2,500/- per flat per month

   - Bank: State Bank of India, Kharghar Branch
   - Account Name: Sunridge Cooperative Housing Society
   - Account Number: 34567890123
   - IFSC Code: SBIN0012345
   - Branch Code: 12345

2. Cheque Payment: Cheques should be drawn in favour of "Sunridge Cooperative Housing Society" and deposited in the drop box kept at the security cabin near the main entrance gate. Please write your flat number and name on the back of the cheque.

3. Cash Payment: Cash payments will be accepted only at the society office between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM from Monday to Saturday. Please collect a receipt for all cash payments. For amounts above Rs. 5,000/-, cash payment will not be accepted as per the society's internal policy.

PAYMENT DEADLINE:

The maintenance fee for each month should be paid on or before the 10th of that month. A late payment penalty of Rs. 100/- per month will be levied for payments received after the 10th, as per the existing bylaws and the Managing Committee's earlier resolution.

Further to our notice No. WSD/PMC/2024/1847 dated 10 August 2024, regarding the planned water supply shutoff on 15 August 2024, we write to provide you with additional details about the repair work. Water Supply Department of PMC cited water_shutoff_reason as pipeline repair; this remains the sole reason for the scheduled interruption.

The repair work involves the replacement of a damaged section of the main water distribution pipeline running along the eastern boundary of your society. The damaged section, approximately 12 metres in length, has been showing signs of leakage for the past several weeks. Our inspection team identified two visible cracks and one joint failure in this stretch. The pipeline is a 300 mm diameter cast iron line installed in 1998, and the affected portion has reached the end of its serviceable life.

Scope of Work:

1. Excavation of the pipeline trench at the identified location.
2. Removal of the damaged pipe section.
3. Installation of new ductile iron pipe section with appropriate joints.
4. Pressure testing of the repaired section.
5. Refilling and compaction of the trench.
6. Restoration of the road surface.

The work will be carried out by our authorised contractor, M/s. Joshi Infrastructure Works, who has been engaged for this project. The contractor will deploy a team of eight workers and one supervisor at the site. All necessary safety precautions, including barricading and warning signage, will be maintained during the work.

We expect the repair work to be completed within the scheduled time of 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM on 15 August 2024. However, due to the nature of underground work, unforeseen conditions such as additional pipe damage or water logging in the trench may cause a delay. In such an event, the water supply will be restored as soon as the repair is completed and the pipeline is tested. The ward office will keep your society informed through the notice board or through your designated contact person.

All residents are requested to cooperate with the contractor's team and not to interfere with the ongoing work. For safety reasons, residents are advised to keep children and pets away from the work site. Vehicle movement in the affected area may be restricted during the excavation and refilling work.

We regret the inconvenience caused to the residents due to this essential maintenance work. This repair is part of the ongoing efforts by the Pune Municipal Corporation to improve the water supply infrastructure in the area and to reduce leakages.
